editorial.headline: Sport and Recreation Training, With a Clear Bali PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers structured sports and recreation instruction—from camps to online coaching—open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for organised instruction in sport and recreation: the kind of teaching that gives participants a deliberate learning structure, an instructor relationship and a defined programme. It can be delivered through a camp, a school-style setting, a training facility belonging to either organiser or client, an educational institution, or online. Day and overnight sports camps sit comfortably within the scope, as do programmes in team sports, gymnastics, riding, swimming, climbing, surfing, martial arts, yoga, card and board games, and esports.

The essential character is educational rather than merely recreational. A professional instructor, teacher, coach or assistant coach may provide the training, but the activity is designed around learning. It does not, however, award a formal qualification in the preschool-to-tertiary education system. For a founder, that distinction keeps the focus on a structured teaching offer: a curriculum, coaching relationship and purposeful participant development, whether delivered in person, digitally or through a camp format.

Registration is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Across Indonesia, the PMA status is TERBUKA, allowing foreign ownership up to the full 100%. In practical terms, a foreign investor may hold the entire business nationally. That clarity matters for operators building a sports academy, specialist coaching practice, camp programme or recreation-learning platform: foreign ownership is not limited below full ownership by the national position in this record.

Bali presents a similarly direct result, with an important risk context rather than a prohibition. Its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and at the Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The activity is not blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium, which applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. A PMA sports and recreation training business can therefore register in Bali today under this activity, while recognising that a Large-scale operation falls within the stated higher-risk OSS classification.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned sports-training business, the distinction is clear: nationally fully open, and in Bali not swept into the PMA moratorium.
